data.summary: In the single week before the exam, the student will concentrate on Unit 4 (Contextual Applications of Differentiation), the identified weak area, while also reviewing key derivative concepts needed for the FRQ. All 12 study hours are allocated to focused practice and timed drills.

weeks.focus: Intensive practice of Unit 4 applications and related derivative review
tasks: Do 5 free‑response FRQ prompts on interpreting derivatives in context (4.1) and write complete solutions, then compare with the scoring guide (2 hrs).
Complete 4 related‑rates problems (4.4) from past exams, timing each for 15 min, and check answers using the solution key (2 hrs).
Work through 6 straight‑line motion scenarios (4.2) calculating position, velocity, and acceleration; verify results with a calculator (2 hrs).
Solve 5 applied‑rate‑of‑change questions (4.3) involving economics or biology contexts; create a one‑page summary of strategies (2 hrs).
Review derivative basics: quickly re‑derive the power rule (2.5) and average‑instantaneous rate concepts (2.1‑2.2); do 10 mixed derivative practice problems for speed (2 hrs).

data.final_week_advice: Use the remaining time to take a full‑length practice exam under timed conditions, then focus on any lingering mistakes in Unit 4 before the test day.
